issues.description: Method Client.assembleBookstore: the problem statement and the template indicate assembleBookstore should produce a Bookstore instance (problem statement asks to "Implement assembleBookstore which creates a Bookstore" and the template contains a commented signature `private static func assembleBookstore() -> Bookstore`). In the solution implementation (Sources/BookstoreLib/Client.swift) the function is declared as `private static func assembleBookstore() -> [Book]` (line 31) but the implementation returns `Bookstore(books: books)` (line 57) and the caller in main expects a Bookstore (`let bookstore = assembleBookstore()` at lines 4-5). This mismatch between the declared return type ([Book]) and the actual returned value/expected type (Bookstore) will cause a compilation error and confuses students about the intended API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the assembleBookstore signature consistent with the problem statement and template by changing its return type to Bookstore (e.g. `private static func assembleBookstore() -> Bookstore`) and return the constructed `Bookstore(books: books)`. Ensure callers (Client.main) receive a Bookstore. Alternatively, if the intended design is to return `[Book]`, update the template and problem text to specify a list return type and modify Client.main to construct a Bookstore from the returned array before using `bookstore.books`.
